name: Ambient light sensor
plain: Android reads lux with no prompt; iOS has no public ambient light API.
meaning: Shows whether the person is indoors, outdoors or in the dark.

ios.note: UIScreen.brightness is the only proxy, and it reflects the setting not the room

limits.headline: Can measure room light on Android, but can't on iPhone
limits.user_action: Nothing. On Android it happens when the app uses auto brightness or a light meter feature
can: Measure the light level around an Android phone, up to about 40000 lux
Adjust screen colors or brightness to match the room (Android)
Check the screen brightness setting on iPhone, which does not show the room
cannot: Measure room light on iPhone; no public sensor exists
Learn the room from iPhone brightness, which only shows your setting
Ask you first on Android; no prompt is used
limits.differs: Android shares the light sensor with no prompt. iPhone has no public ambient light sensor.

story.what_it_is: An app can read how bright the light is around your phone.

marketing.name: Light sensor
marketing.pitch: Android's environment sensors let apps read the light level in lux.

story.for_you: You never see it. Your screen brightness and some apps adapt to a dark room or bright sun. It tells apps whether you are indoors, outside or in bed.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to switch to a dark screen or boost contrast in bright light. It also lets analytics guess your context. Researchers have also shown it can leak details about what is on a screen nearby.

use_cases.example: A reader app turns to a warmer, darker page when the room gets dark.
A cycling app raises screen contrast when you ride in bright sun.
A camera app picks a night mode when it senses low light.
A game dims its menu when you play in the dark so it is easier on your eyes.
A smart home app turns lights on when your phone sees that the room is dark.
A tracker uses light levels to guess if you are indoors, outdoors or in bed.

story.android_note: Android reads light in lux with no prompt.
story.ios_note: iPhone has no public light sensor for apps, though the system adjusts brightness itself.
